title: Best Owens Corning shingle series compared for NH roofs
body_markdown:
**Best overall: Owens Corning Duration. Best for modified-asphalt construction: Duration FLEX. Best straightforward architectural alternative: Oakridge. Best slate-style appearance: Berkshire.** For a homeowner-paid roof replacement in Southern New Hampshire, choose the series alongside the tear-off, flashing, ventilation, and decking scope—not before them.


**TL;DR**

- Duration is the best Owens Corning shingle series for NH roofs when you want a conventional architectural-shingle starting point.
- Duration FLEX fits homeowners specifically seeking polymer-modified asphalt; Berkshire fits homeowners prioritizing a slate-style appearance.
- Compare Oakridge and Duration using identical roof replacement scopes, not shingle names alone.
- Prescott Roofing offers residential roof replacement; request an inspection before deciding which shingle belongs on your estimate.


## Why this matters

A shingle comparison answers only part of your roof replacement decision. Water also needs a clear path past valleys, walls, chimneys, and roof edges. The shingles do not replace the flashing beneath those details.

For your 2026 project, ask [Prescott Roofing](https://prescottroofingnh.com/) about a residential roof replacement inspection before settling on a series. Requesting an inspection starts the conversation; it does not mean an appointment is confirmed.

**Prescott Roofing is a residential roof replacement option for Southern New Hampshire homeowners who want an inspection before choosing shingles.** Use the findings to decide what the roof needs, then compare products within that scope.

## What makes the best Owens Corning shingles for NH roofs?

Judge the complete proposed roof, not just the sample board. These criteria explain the order below:

- **Installation fit:** The product must suit the roof slope, deck, and applicable installation instructions.
- **Water-management details:** The estimate must explain underlayment, ice-barrier placement, and flashing—not simply name a shingle.
- **Material construction:** Conventional laminated asphalt and polymer-modified asphalt are different choices; ask what a proposed change accomplishes.
- **Appearance:** Compare the shingle profile and color against the house, not a small digital swatch alone.
- **Estimate clarity:** Compare the same tear-off, deck-repair terms, ventilation work, and cleanup scope across proposals.

## Owens Corning shingle series at a glance

| Series | Best for | Standout feature | Key limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Owens Corning Duration | A conventional architectural-shingle replacement | SureNail reinforced nailing area | Correct fastening and roof details still matter |
| Owens Corning Duration FLEX | Homeowners seeking polymer-modified asphalt | SBS polymer-modified asphalt construction | Material flexibility does not eliminate installation requirements |
| Owens Corning Oakridge | A straightforward architectural-shingle alternative | Laminated, dimensional appearance | Does not offer Duration's SureNail feature |
| Owens Corning Berkshire | Homeowners prioritizing slate-style appearance | Distinctive slate-like profile | Heavier designer construction requires attention to handling and roof suitability |

These are use-case recommendations, not a claim that every series fits every house. Confirm the exact product designation and current manufacturer instructions on your 2026 estimate. A family name alone is not enough to specify the work.

## 1. Owens Corning Duration: best for a standard replacement

Owens Corning Duration is the default starting point for a conventional architectural asphalt roof replacement. Its SureNail feature provides a reinforced nailing area, giving the installer a defined fastening zone. It remains part of an installation system, not a substitute for one.

For a homeowner comparing bids, Duration makes a clear baseline: specify the same series across proposals, then examine everything beneath and around it. That separates a product difference from a scope difference.

**Duration pros:**

- Architectural profile suits a conventional asphalt roof replacement.
- Reinforced nailing area makes the fastening feature identifiable.
- Provides a specific product baseline for comparing contractor estimates.

**Duration cons:**

- The nailing feature cannot correct unsuitable decking or misplaced fasteners.
- Standard Duration is not the same material choice as Duration FLEX.
- Choosing the shingle does not resolve ventilation or flashing decisions.

**Best for:** Homeowners who want a conventional architectural shingle and a clearly defined replacement scope.

**Verdict: Buy Duration when the inspection supports an asphalt replacement and the estimate explains the complete installation.**

## 2. Duration FLEX: best for polymer-modified asphalt

Owens Corning Duration FLEX uses SBS polymer-modified asphalt. SBS means styrene-butadiene-styrene, a polymer used to modify asphalt properties, including flexibility. That material distinction—not the shared Duration name—is the reason to compare it separately.

New Hampshire winters make installation conditions an important question. Do not turn material flexibility into a promise that installation can proceed under any conditions; the manufacturer's instructions still govern handling, fastening, and sealing requirements.

**Duration FLEX pros:**

- Offers a defined material-construction difference from conventional asphalt shingles.
- Combines polymer-modified asphalt with an architectural profile.
- Gives you a specific alternative to discuss when flexibility is a selection priority.

**Duration FLEX cons:**

- Does not remove the need for proper flashing or attic ventilation.
- Does not establish that your particular house needs modified asphalt.
- Requires an explanation of the product change rather than a vague upgrade label.

**Best for:** Homeowners who specifically want polymer-modified asphalt and understand what the contractor is proposing.

Ask the contractor to identify the exact FLEX product in writing. A proposal that says only architectural shingles leaves the material choice unresolved.

**Verdict: Buy Duration FLEX when polymer-modified construction is a deliberate requirement; hold when the proposal gives no reason for the change.**

## 3. Oakridge: best for a straightforward architectural alternative

Owens Corning Oakridge is a laminated architectural asphalt shingle with a dimensional appearance. It belongs in the comparison when you want another conventional architectural option rather than a designer profile or modified-asphalt specification.

Compare Oakridge against Duration using the same roof scope. Otherwise, differences in flashing replacement, tear-off, or ventilation can get mistaken for differences between shingles.

**Oakridge pros:**

- Provides a dimensional alternative to a flat-looking strip-shingle roof.
- Keeps the selection focused on conventional architectural asphalt construction.
- Supports a direct appearance comparison with Duration samples.

**Oakridge cons:**

- Does not include Duration's SureNail feature.
- A familiar architectural appearance does not establish installation quality.
- A shorter proposal can hide unresolved work regardless of the shingle specified.

**Best for:** Homeowners seeking a straightforward architectural option without making polymer modification or a slate-style profile the priority.

If you are replacing an older strip-shingle roof, compare the broader category in this guide to [3-tab shingle alternatives for NH homeowners](https://prescottroofingnh.com/blog/best-3-tab-shingle-alternatives-for-nh-homeowners).

**Verdict: Buy Oakridge when its appearance meets your goal and the written installation scope stands up to comparison.**

## 4. Berkshire: best for a slate-style appearance

Owens Corning Berkshire is a designer asphalt shingle intended to create a slate-like appearance. Choose it for that visual objective, not because the word designer proves a better fit for every New Hampshire roof.

Review a physical sample and the proposed roof details before committing. Its heavier construction also deserves a clear discussion of material handling and suitability for the existing roof.

**Berkshire pros:**

- Creates a slate-style appearance using asphalt shingles.
- Offers a visibly different profile from conventional architectural shingles.
- Makes sense when the roof is a major part of the home's exterior design.

**Berkshire cons:**

- Is not actual slate.
- Heavier construction makes roof suitability and handling relevant questions.
- Appearance alone does not justify leaving flashing or decking work undefined.

**Best for:** Homeowners whose main selection priority is a slate-style roof profile.

**Verdict: Buy Berkshire for a deliberate appearance goal; skip it when a conventional architectural profile already meets your needs.**

## How these series are ranked

Duration ranks first as the conventional architectural starting point. Duration FLEX, Oakridge, and Berkshire follow because each answers a different selection question: modified asphalt, a straightforward architectural alternative, or slate-style appearance.

This 2026 comparison ranks product fit and estimate clarity. It does not assign invented service lives or treat a product warranty as a prediction of how long your installed roof will last.

## What your roof replacement estimate should include

Ask for the same written scope from every contractor. Prescott Roofing offers residential roof replacement; use the inspection discussion to establish which details belong in your proposal before comparing series.

### Tear-off

Tear-off means removing the existing roofing rather than installing new shingles over it. Ask whether removal, disposal, and protection of surrounding property are included. Make sure the proposal identifies what happens to existing roof components.

### Deck repairs

The deck is the wood surface that supports the roofing. Some conditions become visible only after tear-off, so the estimate should explain how concealed damage is documented and how additional work receives your approval.

Roofing quantities are often expressed in squares: **one roofing square equals 100 square feet**, or a **10-foot by 10-foot** area. Ask how measured area and material waste are handled rather than comparing bundle counts alone.

### Water protection

Underlayment sits beneath the shingles; an ice barrier provides additional protection at specified vulnerable areas. Ask where each material goes and which product is specified. Cold-weather planning belongs in the scope, not in a blanket claim that a particular shingle prevents leaks.

### Flashing

Flashing directs water at intersections and penetrations. Step flashing consists of overlapping pieces where a sloped roof meets a wall. Ask which flashing gets replaced, which gets reused, and how the contractor will assess anything proposed for reuse.

### Ventilation

Ask how attic intake and exhaust ventilation will be assessed. Replacing a roof vent without discussing the rest of the ventilation arrangement leaves an important question unanswered.

For your 2026 replacement, ask for these answers before signing. A shingle upgrade changes a product; a clear scope explains what happens to your house.

## Roof slope changes the installation conversation

A steep roof and a low-slope section should not receive an identical explanation just because both appear on the same house. Slope affects whether shingles are suitable and which installation details apply.

A **2:12 slope rises 2 inches over 12 horizontal inches**. That notation describes geometry, not a quality rating. Ask the contractor to identify any low-slope sections and explain their proposed roof covering using the applicable manufacturer instructions and local requirements.

The same distinction applies when comparing [shingle types for steep-slope roofs](https://yourroofhero.com/blog/best-shingle-types-for-steep-slope-georgia-roofs): roof geometry informs product selection, but a Georgia comparison does not establish New Hampshire installation requirements. For your house, the proposal must address its actual slope, intersections, and conditions.

Do not climb onto the roof to measure it yourself. Ask for the measurements and photographs behind the estimate, especially where a porch or addition meets the main roof.

## Which Owens Corning series should you choose?

**Choose Duration as the default comparison point.** Move to Duration FLEX when polymer-modified asphalt is an intentional specification, Oakridge when its architectural profile meets your requirements, or Berkshire when you specifically want a slate-style appearance.

Before approving your 2026 roof replacement, ask the contractor to separate three decisions:

- **Required work:** What must be addressed to install the roof correctly?
- **Product choice:** What changes when you select a different series?
- **Appearance choice:** Which profile and color do you actually prefer?

Prescott Roofing's residential roof replacement service gives Southern New Hampshire homeowners a starting point for that discussion. Request an inspection and ask for a proposal that identifies the shingle series, installation work, exclusions, and process for additional repairs.

## FAQ


**What's the best Owens Corning shingle series for NH roofs?**

Duration is the default recommendation for a conventional architectural asphalt replacement. Choose Duration FLEX for polymer-modified construction or Berkshire when slate-style appearance is the priority.

**Is Duration FLEX better than standard Duration for every NH home?**

No. Duration FLEX provides a different asphalt construction, but that difference does not establish that every home needs it. Ask what the change accomplishes on your particular roof.

**Should I choose Oakridge or Duration for my replacement?**

Compare Oakridge and Duration against the same installation scope. Duration includes SureNail reinforcement; Oakridge is another architectural option. Neither name tells you whether flashing and deck repairs are adequately specified.

**Does Berkshire give me a real slate roof?**

No. Berkshire is an asphalt shingle designed for a slate-like appearance. Review its physical sample and discuss roof suitability before selecting it.

**What should an Owens Corning roof replacement estimate include?**

The estimate should identify the exact shingles, tear-off, deck-repair terms, underlayment, flashing, ventilation work, disposal, and exclusions. It should also explain how you approve additional work.

**Can I choose shingles before the roof inspection?**

You can shortlist shingles before inspection, but finalize the specification after the roof's condition and installation requirements are understood. Appearance alone cannot establish the necessary replacement work.

**Does requesting an inspection mean my appointment is booked?**

No. An inspection request needs confirmation before you treat it as a booked appointment. Confirm the date and access arrangements directly with the contractor.


## One last thing

Ask one question before signing: **If I choose a different shingle series, which installation details change—and which stay the same?** The answer separates an actual scope change from a different sample on the table.

If the proposal changes only the shingle name, you still need the same clear answers about decking, flashing, water protection, and ventilation. Pick the product after those answers are written down.
